title: New vs Returning Customers per Month
description: For each month, count **new customers** (placing their first ever order in that month) vs **returning customers** (who ordered before). Show order_month, customer_type ('New' or 'Returning'), and customer_count.
solution_sql: WITH first_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(order_date)) AS first_month FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id), classified AS (SELECT o.customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS order_month, CASE WHEN DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) = fo.first_month THEN 'New' ELSE 'Returning' END AS customer_type FROM orders o JOIN first_orders fo ON o.customer_id = fo.customer_id) SELECT order_month, customer_type, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customer_count FROM classified GROUP BY order_month, customer_type ORDER BY order_month, customer_type

test_cases.description: Jan: New=2(C1,C2). Feb: New=2(C3,C4), Returning=1(C1). Mar: New=1(C5), Returning=3(C1,C2,C4). Total 5 rows.

hints: First compute each customer's first_month using MIN(order_date) in a CTE, then join back to all orders and use CASE to classify each order-month as New or Returning.
Use COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) in the outer GROUP BY — a customer ordering twice in the same month should still be counted once.
explanation: The first_orders CTE identifies each customer's debut month. The classified CTE labels each order as New (if the order month matches their debut) or Returning. January: C1 and C2 debut → New=2. February: C3 and C4 debut (New=2); C1 returns (Returning=1). March: C5 debuts (New=1); C1, C2, C4 return (Returning=3). This pattern powers monthly acquisition vs retention dashboards.
